title: Pasta Puttanesca
subtitle: Bold tomato sauce with anchovies, olives and capers
excerpt: Pasta puttanesca is a Neapolitan sauce built from pantry staples: anchovies, olives, capers, and tinned tomatoes. The anchovies dissolve into the oil and give the sauce a deep, savoury base without tasting fishy. It comes together in under 25 minutes.
sourceNotes: Puttanesca is a Neapolitan dish documented from the mid-twentieth century. Its name and exact origin are debated, but the combination of preserved ingredients suggests cucina povera roots.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Reheat gently and cook fresh pasta to serve.

content.text: Do not add extra salt to the sauce before tasting. The anchovies, capers, and olives all carry salt. Season only at the end once everything is combined.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil for the pasta.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the anchovies and chilli flakes. Cook for 2 minutes, pressing the anchovies until they dissolve into the oil.
Add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute until pale golden.
Add the tinned tomatoes, capers, and olives. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened a little.
While the sauce simmers, cook the spaghetti according to pack instructions until al dente. Drain, keeping a cup of pasta water.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce. Toss well, adding a splash of pasta water if needed to loosen. Stir in the parsley and serve.

items.cause: Anchovies, olives, and capers were not rinsed.
items.fix: Rinse all three next time; add pasta water to dilute now.

items.cause: Tomatoes were high in liquid and did not reduce enough.
